description: [narrowed from capacity-refusal-stamps-the-full-compose-cooldown-so-a-compose-that-never-ran-blocks-its-gap-for-5-minutes] MEASURED 2026-08-29 19:26-19:53 on the live substrate. gap-to-feature stamps the 5-minute compose cooldown at PICK-START, before feature_compose has run, and never clears it when the compose returns verdict=BUSY stage=capacity. So a compose that NEVER RAN costs its gap a full 5-minute exclusion from the auto-pick candidate set. EVIDENCE (all firsthand): (1) gap-to-feature.ts:2559-2560 stamps gapComposeLastAttemptAt at pick-start with the comment 'covers the whole compose wall time'; (2) gap-to-feature.ts:2539 filters candidates on nowMs - stamp >= GAP_COMPOSE_COOLDOWN_MS (300000, line 29); (3) the same file ALREADY establishes the governing principle at gap-to-feature.ts:2061 -- 'A compose that never RAN is not a compose that FAILED' -- and isNonAttemptComposeResult() (line 2082) correctly protects failed_attempts and category calibration from BUSY. The cooldown stamp was simply never given the same treatment, so the exact defect that comment describes still applies to SELECTION even though it was fixed for CREDIT. (4) Live cadence proves it: gap concept-usage-record-header-comment-contradicts-its-own-code-on-synthetic-credit recorded approach_decisions at 19:26:31.9, 19:31:46.5, 19:36:52.6, 19:41:56.7, 19:47:01.5 -- deltas 5:14.6 / 5:06.1 / 5:04.1 / 5:04.8, i.e. cooldown-limited to the millisecond, not tick-limited. Every one of those picks logged 'non-attempt (failure_kind=- verdict=BUSY stage=capacity)'. Zero composes ran. (5) 87 BUSY non-attempts in 30 minutes fleet-wide. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE GAP: the AUTONOMOUS lane has effectiveCap = max(1, cap-1) = 1 slot (compose-slots.ts:214, cap default 2 with one reserved for directed work), and composes run for many minutes -- slot-0 was held by a single light-dispatch-vessel compose from 19:43:09 through at least 19:57, 14+ minutes. During any such hold EVERY autonomous pick returns BUSY, so the picker walks the ranked backlog cooling gap after gap for 5 minutes each without a single compose running. The highest-priority gap is repeatedly selected, repeatedly refused for capacity, and repeatedly penalised in SELECTION for it. This is also why the human-escalation escape valve cannot convert: an exempted gap wins the top pick on score (measured 1.275 vs runner-up 1.125) and still never reaches a compose. FIX: on a non-attempt compose result, clear the cooldown stamp (gapComposeLastAttemptAt.delete(gapId)) so the gap is immediately re-eligible -- reuse the existing isNonAttemptComposeResult predicate rather than re-deriving the BUSY test (law 3). DO NOT raise COMPOSE_MAX_CONCURRENT: it is env-gated (law 1), it is a host resource guardrail, and changing the cap has previously inverted the directed/autonomous lanes. DO NOT let this change bump failed_attempts or touch category calibration on BUSY -- that accounting is CORRECT today and must survive the fix. TEST BOTH DIRECTIONS: a BUSY result must leave the gap immediately re-pickable, and a genuine compose (landed or failed) must still cool for the full 5 minutes.
